description: Phase 7: Add daily auto-scheduler that sends artist Instagram previews to Telegram at 16:00 Berlin time. Day 1 after a show → first artist (by sort_order), Day 2 → second artist, etc.

steps.task: Add `check_artist_preview_schedule` function in a new file `source/backend/src/scheduler.rs`. This function takes `state: Arc<AppState>` and performs the scheduling logic: (1) Get current date in Europe/Berlin timezone via chrono-tz. (2) Query all shows where `date < today AND date >= today - 30 days` (reasonable lookback). (3) For each show: compute `days_since = (today - show.date).num_days()`. (4) Fetch artists assigned to the show ordered by `sort_order, name`. (5) If `days_since >= 1 AND days_since <= artist_count`: get the artist at index `days_since - 1`. (6) Check that artist.telegram_artist_preview_sent_at IS NULL (not already sent). (7) Check that artist.instagram_caption IS NOT NULL (caption must exist). (8) Call `telegram_notify::send_artist_instagram_preview(state, &artist)`. (9) Log success or failure.

decisions: 30-day lookback window — beyond that, no more auto-sending
Guard: telegram_artist_preview_sent_at IS NULL prevents re-sends across restarts
Guard: instagram_caption IS NOT NULL ensures we have content to preview
Index is days_since - 1 (day 1 → index 0 → first artist)
learnings: chrono-tz 0.10 should already be in Cargo.toml from a previous plan
Show has a 'date' field (TEXT in SQLite, parsed as NaiveDate or String)
knowledge.notes: Parse show.date carefully — check if it's stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD' or full ISO datetime

steps.task: Register scheduler.rs as a module. Add `pub mod scheduler;` in main.rs alongside existing mod declarations.

learnings: Existing modules in main.rs: ai, audio, auth, config, db, error, image_overlay, models, storage, telegram, telegram_notify, video, etc.

steps.task: Add the daily scheduler background task in main.rs. Following the pattern of the existing weekly expired-user-cleanup (lines 487-510): add a `tokio::spawn` block that runs a loop with `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(60))`. On each tick: get current time in Europe/Berlin. Check if the minute is :00 and the hour is 16 (i.e., exactly 16:00). If so, call `scheduler::check_artist_preview_schedule(state.clone()).await`. Use a simple `last_check_date` variable to ensure it only runs once per day (compare current date to last_check_date, only proceed if different).

decisions: last_check_date guard prevents multiple runs if the 60s window catches 16:00 twice
Check hour == 16 in Berlin timezone, not UTC
learnings: Existing pattern at lines 487-510: tokio::spawn + interval loop
knowledge.notes: For development/testing, consider adding an env var SCHEDULER_DISABLED=true to skip the scheduler, or add a Telegram command to manually trigger it

steps.task: Run `cargo check` from source/backend/ to verify Phase 7 compiles. Fix any compilation errors.
